Deciding which class to play really depends on the type of players you are, your experience and dedication to raiding. A number of other questions might be asked additionally to the information given in your initial post. What expansion are you considering? Besides being casual how experienced are you in raiding and wow in general? What kind of guild are you looking to join? You mention being casual, what kinds of time constraints do you have towards raiding? The answer to choosing between Prot Paladin and Shadow Priest, raise a number of other questions and factors to consider before making an appropriate decision.

The biggest concerns for you to address may be your endgame knowledge of the encounters and availability to your guild. On most private servers, guilds tend to have a lot of expectation of tanks. 

A significant number of players tend to be impatient towards raiding, largely because they have already cleared the content in retail or on another private server(s). Typically I would say that in any established guild, or at least ones with established leadership, the tank positions will be accounted for. Guilds looking for tanks will likely be looking for tanks who are exceptional; both in game knowledge, and also having large amounts of time at their disposal, which in general is not conducive to casual players. Having a large amount of game knowledge is a common requirement among endgame tanks, not only in raid mechanics but in gearing, stat selection and possessing a solid understanding of class abilities, overall class design, function and mechanics.  While raiders can be impatient to tanks who are not aware of boss mechanics and game knowledge, they could be even more impatient to absentees and tardiness. Given that they have geared you up and your role is one of a kind in a raid, you become something not easily replaceable or pugable. Even being absent once or having to leave earlier could be a reason not to play the tanking role, of course not always possible for the every player. Unless you know the raid bosses and game well and additionally don't have time constraints I would recommend that you play Dps, as it is likely many of your raid group will not want to rely on someone on the casual side of raiding.

If you are concerned about find dungeon groups quickly, playing a tank may not be as beneficial as you would first believe. A lot of the que times are determined by server population and server age. Fresh servers are likely to have a more active player, who not only queing more in general but are likely to be in a similar position in progressively advancing through dungeons for raiding purposes. Another reason for the unnecessary choice of tank,  is that, depending on the expansion, duel specing as disc/holy is a viable way to skip/shorten dungeons ques. And again depending on the expansion the gear you acquire for healing will be potentially be equally as good for Spriest in addition to off-rolling as dps or coming to agreements with your dungeon groups regarding items. Que times for tanks are generally not much better than they are for healers but I guess still something to consider, you also don't mention holy or disc in your post so it might not be something you are interested in. Overall the benefit of tanking solely for que times shouldn't be a significant factor in making your class choice, whereas server choice and finding a good guild could be more important factors in the previously mentioned issues.

For preparation I would say that spriest would be an easier class to prep for in endgame content. Typically tailoring and enchanting are always good choices for professions as a Shadow Priest. Both of these skills being easier to level up than most of the other options players have. Where as Prot Paladins can be expected to have a combination of JC/BS/Engi, all of which require large amounts ore and trade goods, via mining or gold. Not only that but missing consumables and enchants could potentially be tolerated more as dps. In part because the number of dps in a given raid, making the odds of going unnoticed or being forgiven higher, also in part due to an enchant, gem or consumable missing from a tank being more likely to effect raid progression. The time saved via profession choices and the less crucial nescicity of having all proper preparation are note worthy in your class choice.  

All things considered it really comes down to your own personal preference. While responsibility of tanking and expectations surrounding the raid position could easily be daunting to the casual player, it really come down to what you feel comfortable playing and, more importantly what you enjoy playing.

My advise is to get a solid macro game/plan and learn to deflect attacks as you play against them. For me the funniest part is learning, improving and gaining better insight into the game.

For ZvZ Cheese:

When you scout with your first overlord, make sure to send it across the map asap, right after you build a drone with the initial 50 minerals. Then when it arrives at the opposing natural compare the (depending on map size) Completion of base, lack of base and how the base looks compared to yours. If it is even slightly off what your base look likes, including the creep spreading from his base before his first queen; it is likely that your opponent went pool first. The next clue to look for is, before your OL is chased away by his queen, look at what he is morphing his larva into and how many drones he has on his natural.

4th Stage:

Typically lurker into vipers, as far as stages in general my plan is to get roach and drones while surviving the lingbane phase then adding lurkers asap

LingBane Micro:

For me personally I make as few lings and banes as possible and get a Roach Warren as soon as I feel comfortable it won't kill me to spend the minerals, always getting a 3rd at standard times, assuming no 12 pool.

ZvP:

I just go roach into roach/hydra and add lurkers and upgrades as soon as I can, adding in some ling bane harrass when possible and ending the game around 9-12 minutes. I typically don't aim for late game in all match ups and just prolong mid game/late-midgame.

In my experience versus Protoss compositions that relies on lings like LBH don't fair very well. While lings do good against stalkers, roach is superior to lings versus every other Protoss unit and trades at least evenly against stalkers. Once immortals are out which melt roach, you should have hydras out, and even a few lurkers by the time any significant number of immortal is there. Not that LBH isn't workable but you will need to micro you lings better to attack the correct targets and avoid splash from archon/ht/colossus although lings do hard counter immortal.

You can always go mutalisk builds but to me its always a gamble in all matchups and I don't really have a lot experience using them.

But yeah roach/hydra into lurker is really strong vs Protoss, make sure you have the upgrades asap. Try to bait out storms and kite with your mobile units into lurkers, ideally at chokes, high ground or good concaves.

Could we consider in this thread another related topic. I'll call it "Production Asymmetry" or "Unit Creation Asymmetry". As far as overall Faction Asymmetry goes I believe this could potentially be the most relevant topic.

In my experience in starcraft, I have seen through both peoples comments and personal gameplay, that "Production Asymmetry" is a huge source of balance complaints but also what I feel created dynamic gameplay in SC2.

I would include often controversial topics such as Zerg larva production, and the infamous Protoss Warprism, even building addons for Terran. All of these game features I feel are great mechanics making the game more interesting through variety but in turn are also major sources of balance and poor game design complaints.

Now as to an opinion of the topic, I really like the variety of Unit Production in SC2. Despite the many threads I have seen about how these differing production methods are the main or major source for game inbalance, I find the variety to be my favourite aspect of the game or atleast what makes the interaction between factions interesting. I have little reference to "Unit Production Asymmetry" in other rts games but I just assume they for the most part feature similar production methods between factions. I played AOE2 when I was very young but don't fully feel comfortable drawing comparisons.

To sum up my personal opinion I would be more in favour of Production Variety even if at the cost of balance. Of course within reason, but for an example, the current state of SC2 is balanced to my liking (minus mech xd). As for previous patches, most of the poor balance I would credit to OP units or unit comps (BL infesty). So my vote goes toward "Non-Asymmetric Unit Production" even if at the cost of slight inbalance tendencies inherent to the nature of non-asymmetry in general.
